title: Angular geometry on the actual unit sphere
source_anchor: Samplinglib original sphere geometry and feature-law supplement v1, 2026-10-23; exact units[0] and complete formula proof
target_statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, and let S be its literal unit-norm subtype. The actual angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)) is jointly continuous and measurable on S×S. For every pair it lies between zero and pi, equals Mathlib's unoriented vector angle, dominates the ambient chord norm, vanishes exactly on the diagonal, and is symmetric. It satisfies the triangle inequality. These are explicit properties of the angular cost; no inherited chord-distance instance is replaced, no path-length geodesic-distance identification or Wasserstein theorem is included, and no sphere nonemptiness or positive dimension is assumed.
